paper.title: Multi-Armed Bandits With Machine Learning-Generated Surrogate Rewards

unmapped: Each pull also reveals a surrogate (ML-predicted) reward; true and surrogate rewards are jointly bivariate Gaussian with unknown means, variances and correlation rho_k (|rho_k|<1)
Learner has an offline pool of N_k i.i.d. surrogate rewards per arm; surrogate means may be arbitrarily biased
settings.definition_quote: In the online phase, if the arm $k$ is pulled for the $s$-th time, the decision maker can observe a surrogate reward $\hat{R}_{k, s}$ alongside a true reward $R_{k, s}$ ... In the offline phase, the decision maker has access to a static pool of surrogate rewards $\{\hat{R}_{k,s}^\off\}_{s=1}^{N_k}$ for arm $k$. ... we assume that the true and surrogate rewards are bivariate Gaussian with unknown mean and covariance matrix

settings.name_in_paper: MAB with batched reward (non-Gaussian) and surrogate rewards
unmapped: Each pull deploys the arm to a batch of m i.i.d. units, yielding m pairs of true and surrogate rewards (not the classical limited-adaptivity batched bandit)
Offline pool of m*N_k i.i.d. surrogate rewards per arm
Rewards, surrogates and projection residuals sub-Gaussian with normalized psi_2 norm <= L and bounded skewness ratios; variances and sub-Gaussian norms unknown to learner
Local regime sigma_k^2/(m Delta_k^2) = Omega(1), sigma_max/sigma_min = O(1), m >= 8 (ln T)^4 etc. (Assumption 2)
settings.definition_quote: If $A_t=k$, then arm $k$ is deployed to $m$ independent units in that round and we observe a new batch of $m$ i.i.d. pairs of true and surrogate rewards ... the cumulative regret over $T$ decision rounds is $\mathrm{Reg}_T=\sum_{t=1}^T m(\mu^\star-\mu_{A_t})$

source.label: thm: lower bound
source.quote: Under the Gaussian data generation model \eqref{eqn: gaussian model}, let $\pi$ be any uniformly good policy as defined in Definition \ref{def: uniformly good policy}, then $\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb E_\theta^\pi[\mathrm{Reg}_T]}{\ln T}\ge\sum_{k\ne k^\star}\frac{2\Delta_k}{\ln\lb1+\dfrac{\Delta_k^2}{\sigma_k^2(1-\rho_k^2)}\rb}$.

results.notes: Holds regardless of offline sample size (proof uses only the online likelihood).
